{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient / AP)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Exhibit 10.14 Master Services Agreement, dated 5 February 

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 19 rule positions. The commercial architecture is broadly favourable to us: the Agreement is expressly non-exclusive, imposes no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-compete, no non-solicit, no audit right and no liquidated damages on us, and the Vendor indemnity (with warranties covering IP non-infringement, data security and compliance with Law, and an indemnity carve-out from the consequential-damages waiver) sits at or above our preferred position. Governing law (Delaware) and venue (New York courts) sit at the fallback and are acceptable.

Six items require attention. Three are critical or high-severity structural gaps: (i) there is **no monetary liability cap anywhere** in the document, so direct liability is unlimited in both directions and the fallback is not met; (ii) there is **no IP or data ownership provision**, leaving our Content, Properties and visitor data unallocated; and (iii) the Auction Platform **licence is revocable at will and excludes our affiliates and contractors** with no path to add them — the playbook's walk-away case. In addition, the auto-renewal opt-out window is effectively 90 days (fallback is 60), there is **no transition assistance or data-return obligation** (the current "return or destroy" election permits Kubient to unilaterally destroy our data), and there is **no vendor insurance obligation at all** despite Kubient hosting the platform and storing visitor data.

We have prepared redlines for each deviation and each missing clause; no compliant clause has been reopened.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | Preamble (Section 7) | No monetary cap anywhere; direct liability unlimited both ways, failing the 12-month fallback. Carve-out structure (indemnity, confidentiality) is acceptable and mutual. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | Preamble | No IP or data ownership provision; § 14(b) covers only names/marks. No ownership statement for our data and no licence to deliverables. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 10–11, 7(a), 9(b)) | Broad Vendor defend/indemnify covering Services, Platform, Creative, warranty breach and acts/omissions; no infringement carve-outs; no super-cap. At or above preferred. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble (para 2; cf. 8(a), 14(h)) | Grant is unqualifiedly "revocable" and names Customer only; § 8(a) bars third-party access absent consent. This is the rule's walk-away case. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble (§ (h)) | Mutual successor/affiliate/M&A assignment with reasonable-consent backstop; no change-of-control right for Kubient. At fallback. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) | Exclusivity expressly disclaimed; we remain free to use other agents or sell directly. Preferred position. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Preamble (4(a), 7(a)) | No LDs, penalty or early-termination fee on us; § 4(a) is earned revenue share only. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory restriction on us. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 4, 5) | 1-year Initial Term; mutual 90-day convenience right thereafter; no early-termination fee. Sits at fallback. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Deviation** | Preamble | Automatic 1-year renewals with no non-renewal mechanic; effective opt-out is the 90-day convenience notice, failing the 60-day fallback. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Preamble (para 4(c)) | No transition assistance, no data export in usable format, no deletion certification; "return or destroy" election sits with Kubient. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) | No vendor audit, inspection or records right; only a service-enablement cooperation covenant. Better than preferred. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | Preamble (Section 14(a); cf. Section 8) | Delaware law (accepted/fallback), exclusive New York courts. Section 8 AAA arbitration is in tension with the forum clause — clean-up point only. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | Preamble | No MFN in either direction. Preferred position. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1, para p0023) | Per-Exhibit engagement, revenue share on amounts actually generated; no committed spend or shortfall mechanic. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant on us. Preferred position. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | Preamble (Section 9(b); Section 13) | Express performance, malicious-code and compliance-with-Law warranties running for the Term; the disclaimer is twice qualified and reaches implied warranties only. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble (Section 14) | No insurance obligation on either party, despite Kubient hosting the Platform and storing visitor data. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following three items fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Licence revocability and scope (para 2).** A licence that Kubient may revoke at its discretion, combined with the § 8(a) bar on third-party access, means our affiliates and contractors cannot lawfully use the Platform and our access can be withdrawn at will. Our redline extends the licence to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (with us responsible for their compliance), limits revocation to expiration or termination under para 4, and conforms transferability to § 14(h).
2. **Data destruction on termination (para 4(c)).** The current election allows Kubient to destroy rather than return our Content, Requests, reporting and visitor data. Our redline inserts transition assistance, machine-readable return within 30 days, and certified deletion.
3. **No insurance at all (Section 14).** Kubient hosts the Platform and, per § 9(b)(iii), collects, manages and stores visitor data with no coverage behind it. Our redline inserts CGL (USD 1M/2M), E&O (USD 2M), cyber (USD 5M) and workers' compensation, with certificates on request; the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is available.

We also treat the **absence of any liability cap** as a gating item, though for a different reason: it fails the fallback outright and leaves both parties exposed to unlimited direct liability.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six open items: liability cap (Section 7), IP/data ownership (new clause), licence scope (para 2), non-renewal right (renewal sentence), transition and data return (para 4(c)), and insurance (new § 14(j)).
2. **Liability cap — proposed position.** Because Section 5 is a revenue share under which Kubient pays us, a cap keyed to "fees paid by Customer" would be illusory. We propose a mutual cap on amounts paid or payable between the parties with a USD 1,000,000 floor, uncapped Excluded Claims, and revenue-share amounts owed under Section 5 expressly outside the cap.
3. **Renewal — fallback authority.** Our ask is a 30-day Customer non-renewal right, leaving the mutual 90-day convenience right untouched; a 60-day window is acceptable if pressed.
4. **IP/data ownership — drafting brief.** We retain all rights in our Content, Properties and Customer Data; Kubient retains its platform and background IP; deliverables are assigned to us with a licence-back to embedded Kubient IP; joint ownership excluded.
5. **Clean-up pass.** Align the Section 8 AAA arbitration provision with the Section 14(a) exclusive court-jurisdiction language. Neither triggers a walk-away, but the inconsistency should be resolved before signature.
6. **Exhibit diligence.** Each Exhibit should be checked for minimum volume or spend language and for any audit or system-access rights, neither of which appears in the master and neither of which we would accept without the preferred parameters.

We have not redlined any clause classified as compliant, including those sitting at the fallback (assignment, governing law, termination for convenience)."}
